extracted.intended_audience: Users, developers and system administrators installing or configuring PARI/GP (power users of the gp calculator and libpari)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP: descriptions of gp functions (including parallel functions), the GP defaults (toggles and formatting options), and instructions/options for configuring, compiling, and testing PARI/GP on Unix-like systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: warning({str}*)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs the message “user warning” and the argument list (each of them interpreted as a string). If colors are enabled, this warning will be in a different color, making it easy to distinguish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: warning(n, " is very large, this might take a while.")

rubrics_metrics.name: whatnow(key)
rubrics_metrics.description: If keyword key is the name of a function that was present in GP version 1.39.15 or lower, outputs the new function name and syntax, if it changed at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to find new names/syntax for obsolete functions (387 out of 560 changed). See Section 3.12.41 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: write(filename, {str}*)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writes (appends) to filename the remaining arguments, and appends a newline (same output as print).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: void gpwrite(const char *filename, ...) . Equivalent to print with a trailing newline.

rubrics_metrics.name: write1(filename, {str}*)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writes (appends) to filename the remaining arguments without a trailing newline (same output as print1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: similar to write but omits the newline; useful for incremental output.

rubrics_metrics.name: writebin(filename, {x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Writes (appends) to filename the object x in binary format. The format is not human readable but contains the exact internal structure of x and is faster to save/load than a string expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary files include a magic number for recognition. If x is omitted, saves all user variables with names (reading restores variables). Binary files are architecture-dependent and not recommended for long-term storage; gzip compression allowed; installed functions and history objects cannot be saved via this function. Library syntax: void gpwritebin(const char *filename, GEN x = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: writetex(filename, {str}*)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writes the remaining arguments to filename in TeX format (like write but in TeX format).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to generate TeX-formatted logs or output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel interfaces supported
rubrics_metrics.description: Two multithread interfaces supported: POSIX threads and Message Passing Interface (MPI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POSIX threads are well-suited for single systems; MPI is used by most clusters. Properly written GP programs will work identically with either engine (the parallel GP interface is engine-agnostic).

rubrics_metrics.name: parapply(f, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel evaluation of f on the elements of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The function f must not access global variables or variables declared with local(), and must be free of side effects. Example: parapply(factor, [2^256+1,2^193-1]). Library syntax: GEN parapply(GEN f, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: pareval(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel evaluation of the elements of x, where x is a vector of closures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closures must be arity 0, must not access global variables or variables declared with local, and must be free of side effects. Library syntax: GEN pareval(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: parfor(i = a, {b}, expr1, {j}, {expr2})
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates expr2 for i between a and b in random order, computed in parallel; in expr2 substitute j by the value of expr1 (which may depend on i). If b is omitted the loop will not stop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: expr2 may use break/next/return but if used, expr2 will still be evaluated for remaining values of i less than the current one unless another break/next/return occurs. Side-effect-free code recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: parforprime(p = a, {b}, expr1, {j}, {expr2})
rubrics_metrics.description: Like parfor but iterates p over primes between a and b in random order and substitutes j by expr1 (dependent on p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same semantics about break/next/return as parfor. Use for parallel prime-indexed loops.

rubrics_metrics.name: parselect(f, A, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Selects elements of A according to the selection function f, done in parallel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag is 1, return the indices of those elements (indirect selection). The function f must not access global variables or variables declared with local(), and must be free of side effects. Library syntax: GEN parselect(GEN f, GEN A, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: parsum(i = a, b, expr, {x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Sum of expression expr, initialized at x, with the formal parameter i going from a to b, evaluated in parallel in random order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expression expr must not access global variables or variables declared with local(), and must be free of side effects. Example: parsum(i=1,1000, ispseudoprime(2^prime(i)-1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: parvector(N, i, expr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Like vector(N,i,expr) but the evaluations of expr are done in parallel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expression expr must not access global variables or variables declared with local(), and must be free of side effects. Example: parvector(10,i,quadclassunit(2^(100+i)+1).no).

rubrics_metrics.name: TeXstyle default
rubrics_metrics.description: Bits controlling less rigid TeX formatting commands in the gp logfile (only used when log = 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bit meanings: 2 = insert \right/\left pairs where appropriate; 4 = insert discretionary breaks in polynomials. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: breakloop default
rubrics_metrics.description: If true, enables the “break loop” debugging mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is 1 for interactive gp sessions and 0 otherwise. See Section 2.10.3 for debugging details.

rubrics_metrics.name: colors default
rubrics_metrics.description: Controls colored output when gp runs in color-capable terminals. Accepted values: strings "a1,...,ak" with k ≤ 7 where each ai is either the keyword no, an integer 0–15, or a triple [c0,c1,c2] for foreground/background/attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The seven affected outputs are error messages, history numbers, prompt, input line, output, help messages, timer. If k<7 remaining ai assumed no. Special presets: darkbg, lightbg, boldfg. Incompatible with PariEmacs (change will fail silently). Example default: "" (no colors); example setting: default(colors, "9, 5, no, no, 4").

rubrics_metrics.name: compatible default (0..3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Backward compatibility modes for GP function names and syntax (values 0–3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: compatible=0: no backward compatibility (recommended). compatible=1: warn when using obsolete functions but accept them (cannot disable warning). compatible=2: use only the old function naming scheme (case sensitive differences apply). compatible=3: try to mimic exactly former behavior (not always possible). Changing between groups {0,1} and {2,3} can erase user functions/aliases (variables unaffected). Recommendation: switch to compatible=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: datadir default
rubrics_metrics.description: Name of directory containing optional data files (elldata, galdata, galpol, seadata packages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is the GP share/pari path (location of installed precomputed data). Can be specified at Configure time via --datadir=. Example default given in manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: debug default
rubrics_metrics.description: Debugging level; if non-zero, extra messages may be printed according to activity (see \g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is 0 (no debugging messages).

rubrics_metrics.name: debugfiles default
rubrics_metrics.description: File usage debugging level; if non-zero gp will print information on file descriptors in use from PARI’s point of view (see \gf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: debugmem default
rubrics_metrics.description: Memory debugging level; if non-zero gp will regularly print memory usage. If >2 it indicates garbage collection events and the function where they occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant slowdown; memory usage output disabled unless running a version compiled for debugging. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: echo default
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle (1/0). When echo mode is on each command is reprinted before being executed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when reading files with \r or read commands. Used in test files checking gp builds. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: factor_add_primes toggle
rubrics_metrics.description: If on, integer factorization machinery calls addprimes on primes factor that were difficult to find (larger than 2^24), so they are automatically tried first in other factorizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows recovery of found prime factors if interrupted, but a huge addprimes table can slow down arithmetic functions that rely on factorization; empty the table with removeprimes. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: factor_proven toggle
rubrics_metrics.description: If on, factors output by integer factorization machinery are tested/proven prime, making dependent results fully proven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not affect partial factorizations explicitly requested, and does not change entries in the private addprimes table. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: format default (x.n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Controls printing of real numbers: conversion style x ∈ {e,f,g} and precision n (number of significant digits or all digits if n<0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: e: scientific format with explicit exponent; f: fixed floating format (large numbers with unknown integer part printed in e); g: non-zero printed in f unless decimal exponent < −4 then e, zeroes printed in e. Default: "g.28" on 32-bit and "g.38" on 64-bit machines. Use printf/Strprintf for more control.

rubrics_metrics.name: graphcolormap default
rubrics_metrics.description: A vector of colors for hi-res graphing routines; length arbitrary but at least 3 (background, frame/ticks, axes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colors may be strings (from rgb.txt, lowercase, no whitespace) or RGB code vectors [r,g,b] with integers 0–255. All colors may be used in plotcolor calls. Example default vector provided in manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: graphcolors default
rubrics_metrics.description: Indices into graphcolormap used to plot multi-curves; successive curves use graphcolormap[graphcolors[1]], graphcolormap[graphcolors[2]], ... cycling when exhausted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is [4,5].

rubrics_metrics.name: help default
rubrics_metrics.description: Name/path of external help program to use from within gp when extended help is invoked (?? or ??? or M-H under readline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is the path to the gphelp script installed with GP.

rubrics_metrics.name: histfile default
rubrics_metrics.description: Filename where gp will keep history of input commands (results omitted). If this file exists when histfile changes it is read in and becomes part of session history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting this default in gprc saves readline history between sessions. Empty string "" changes it to <undefined>. Default value is <undefined>.

rubrics_metrics.name: histsize default
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of last results gp keeps in history and which can be recovered using % notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When exceeded oldest values are erased. Default value is 5000. If set to a positive value, gp prints at most that many lines per result (see lines default).

rubrics_metrics.name: lines default
rubrics_metrics.description: If set to a positive value, gp prints at most that many lines from each result, terminating last shown line with [+++] if further material was suppressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print commands (print, \a) unaffected allowing viewing of full result. If screen width unknown, a line is assumed to be 80 characters. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: linewrap default
rubrics_metrics.description: If set to a positive value, gp wraps every single printed line after that many characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is 0 (unset).

rubrics_metrics.name: log default (0..3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Logging mode: 0 off, 1 plain logfile, 2 emit color codes to logfile, 3 write LaTeX output to logfile (customizable by TeXstyle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When on, gp opens a logfile (name controlled by logfile default) and appends commands and results. If a file with the exact name already exists it is appended, not overwritten. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: logfile default
rubrics_metrics.description: Name of the log file used when logging is enabled; environment and time expansion performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is "pari.log".

rubrics_metrics.name: nbthreads default
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of threads to use for parallel computing; exact meaning depends on the chosen mt engine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For single engine: not used (always one thread). For pthread engine: number of threads (unlimited, default: number of cores). For mpi engine: number of MPI processes to use (limited by mpirun allocation, default: use all allocated processes).

rubrics_metrics.name: new_galois_format toggle
rubrics_metrics.description: If on, polgalois command uses a different, more consistent, naming scheme for Galois groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided so scripts can control behavior and avoid breakage. Default 0; will change to 1 in next major version.

rubrics_metrics.name: output default (0/1/3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three possible output formats: 0 = raw (input-like, machine-friendly), 1 = prettymatrix (matrices printed as boxes, prettier but not usable for input), 3 = external prettyprint (pipes gp output in TeX to external prettyprinter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Column vectors still printed horizontally in prettymatrix. Use commands \a, \m, \B to force formats at any time. Default value is 1 (prettymatrix).

rubrics_metrics.name: parisize default
rubrics_metrics.description: Stack size in bytes required by gp and libpari to perform computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended to increase this default (via -s or gprc) if possible, but do not exceed installed RAM to avoid paging. In emergency use allocatemem to increase parisize once session started. Default value: 4M on 32-bit, 8M on 64-bit machines.

rubrics_metrics.name: path default
rubrics_metrics.description: List of directories gp searches for non-absolute filenames (colon-separated on UNIX, semicolon on Windows/DOS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order is respected; environment expansion performed. Common default: ".:~:~/gp" on UNIX, ".;C:\;C:\GP" on DOS/Windows, "." otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: prettyprinter default
rubrics_metrics.description: Name of external prettyprinter to use when output=3 (alternate prettyprinter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is "tex2mail -TeX -noindent -ragged -by par". The default tex2mail looks better than built-in beautified format (output=2).

rubrics_metrics.name: primelimit default
rubrics_metrics.description: GP precomputes primes less than primelimit at initialization and can build fast sieves to iterate primes up to primelimit^2; used by many arithmetic functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximal values depend on machine word size; PARI guarantees first 6547 primes (up to 65557) are precomputed even if primelimit=1. This default is only used at startup (changing it later does not recompute). Deprecated uses are noted; default value is 500k.

rubrics_metrics.name: prompt default
rubrics_metrics.description: String printed as the gp prompt; supports usual escape sequences and time expansion via strftime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \e for Esc, \n for newline, \\ for backslash. If using readline, brace escape sequences with \[ and \] to avoid display bugs. PariEmacs needs to know the prompt pattern to separate input from prior results. Default example: "?\n" (document shows a prompt string).

rubrics_metrics.name: prompt_cont default
rubrics_metrics.description: String printed as continuation prompt for continuation lines (e.g., between braces or after line-terminating backslash).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Everything that applies to prompt also applies to prompt_cont. Default value is "".

rubrics_metrics.name: psfile default
rubrics_metrics.description: Default filename where gp dumps PostScript drawings; data appended so previous data not lost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environment and time expansion performed. Default value is "pari.ps".

rubrics_metrics.name: readline default
rubrics_metrics.description: Switch to enable/disable GNU readline line-editing facilities for gp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disabling can be useful if gp is run inside terminals that interact badly with readline. When disabled, advanced editing features like automatic completion and history are not available. Default value is 1 (on).

rubrics_metrics.name: realprecision default
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of significant digits used to convert exact inputs given to transcendental functions or to create absolute floating point constants; also used internally for t_REAL numbers (format may override printing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PARI internal precision works on a word basis; reported default(realprecision) shows internal significant digits, not displayed digits. Example: default(realprecision,2) results in 19 internal significant digits on a 64-bit machine but displays 2. Defaults: 38 on 64-bit, 28 on 32-bit.

rubrics_metrics.name: recover default
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle (1/0). If set to 0 any error becomes fatal and causes gp to exit immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful in batch scripts to ensure failures stop execution. Default value is 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: secure default
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle (1/0). If on, the system and extern commands are disabled to prevent executing arbitrary UNIX commands from gp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: gp will ask for confirmation before letting you unset this toggle. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: seriesprecision default
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of significant terms when converting a polynomial or rational function to a power series (\ps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default value is 16.

rubrics_metrics.name: simplify default
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle (1/0). When on, convert result types to the simplest possible types automatically (e.g., rationals to integers when exact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disabling this leaves types as computed; use simplify function to simplify recursively. Default value is 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: sopath default
rubrics_metrics.description: List of directories (colon-separated) where gp will look for shared libraries when installing external symbols if a non-absolute path is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is empty string "" meaning install will use the library name as input and look in current directory if not absolute.

rubrics_metrics.name: strictargs default
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle (1/0). If on, all arguments to new user functions are mandatory unless the function supplies an explicit default value. Otherwise arguments default to 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to functions defined while strictargs is on; changing strictargs does not affect previously defined functions. Example: fun(a,b=2)=a+b; with strictargs on, fun() triggers a missing mandatory argument error. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: strictmatch default
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle (1/0). If on, unused characters after a sequence has been processed will produce an error; otherwise just a warning is printed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when debugging unmatched parentheses in nested code; default value is 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: threadsize default
rubrics_metrics.description: In parallel mode, size in bytes of the private stack for each thread; total allocated memory is parisize + nbthreads × threadsize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If set to 0, the value used is the same as parisize. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: timer default
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle (1/0). When on, every instruction sequence in gp is timed and a timing printed immediately before the output (user CPU time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format: time = N ms. If time < 1 ms nothing is printed. Timing excludes printing time. Default value is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required tools for compiling PARI
rubrics_metrics.description: Compiling PARI requires an ANSI C or a C++ compiler (gcc/g++ recommended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional but useful libraries/programs: GNU MP (faster multiprecision kernel), GNU readline (line editing, completion, history), GNU emacs + PariEmacs, gzip/gunzip/gzcat (read compressed data), perl (extended online help). All are free; download pointers at PARI website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Configure basic usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Run ./Configure in top-level directory to configure PARI/GP; use --prefix to set install prefix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Configure creates a build directory OOSNAME-arch and prints detected architecture, compiler and optimization flags. Look for messages prefixed by ### indicating problems (gmp, readline, X11, perl, gz). Configure creates config.log in the build directory for debugging. If Configure fails try ./Configure -a interactive mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: --tune and advanced Configure flags
rubrics_metrics.description: --tune: fine-tune library for host by running many comparative tests producing tune.h; --graphic=lib: enable particular graphics library (X11 default); --time=function: choose timing function (getrusage, clock_gettime, times, ftime) and --mt=engine: specify parallel engine (single, pthread, mpi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tune can take ~30 minutes and yields ~10% speed boost; tune GMP first if using GMP. --mt=pthread implies --enable-tls. Use --time=ftime when benchmarking multi-threaded code to get wall-clock time rather than summed thread CPU time. Beware ABI changes when using parallel-related flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compilation commands
rubrics_metrics.description: To compile the gp binary and documentation use make all; to compile only gp use make gp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel make (make -jN) in the build directory speeds up compilation. For bench/testing builds, make may build multiple binaries (gp-sta, gp-dyn) and run tests with both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic tests after compilation
rubrics_metrics.description: Run make bench (or make dobench) to test the binary; the bench runs a quick series of tests and may detect problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a [BUG] message appears check files that show differences between test output and expected results; decide if it is a bug in your configuration or PARI and consider reporting it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-compiling guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: When cross-compiling set RUNTEST to a program that can run target binaries (e.g., an emulator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RUNTEST used for both Configure tests and make bench to execute target binaries during build/testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installation directories customization
rubrics_metrics.description: Configure installs gp binary and scripts in $prefix/bin, library in $prefix/lib, include files in $prefix/include/pari, and architecture-independent data under $share_prefix/pari.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can override defaults with --bindir, --libdir, --includedir, --mandir, --datadir, --sysdatadir, and --share-prefix flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment variables for Configure
rubrics_metrics.description: Configure accepts environment variables to override detected tools and to append/prepend flags: CC, DLLD, LD, CFLAGS, CPPFLAGS, LDFLAGS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., env CC=cc Configure to choose a particular compiler. Prepending/appending behavior described in manual; use g++ -fpermissive if forcing a C++ compiler on fussy g++ versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Troubleshooting Configure failures
rubrics_metrics.description: If default Configure run fails, try ./Configure -a (interactive mode) to answer questions; check config.log and messages with ###.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are ~30 questions in interactive mode; accepting all defaults may still fail. If problems persist consider filing a bug report with relevant logs.
